title: NetSuite Accounting Services: Who Runs the Books After Go-Live
summary: NetSuite accounting services, explained. See what an outsourced team runs inside your instance, what it costs per month, and when to keep the work in-house.
body_markdown:
## What NetSuite Accounting Services Cover


NetSuite accounting services are a monthly engagement where an outside accounting team operates inside the NetSuite instance you already license.


The implementation partner’s final invoice is paid. The instance is live. Then the first real month-end arrives and nobody owns the Period Close Checklist. That is the gap this service fills, and it is the reason indinero runs client books in NetSuite, QuickBooks Online, and Xero instead of selling a platform.


This page is not about picking software. If that decision is still open, our[NetSuite vs QuickBooks comparison](https://www.indinero.com/blog/netsuite-vs-quickbooks/) covers usage limits, OneWorld, and the graduation triggers. This one starts the day after.


### The monthly scope of work


Generic accounting verbs tell a controller nothing. Here is the work named against the NetSuite objects an operator actually touches.


- **Transaction processing.** Vendor bill entry and approval routing, payment scheduling, 1099 tracking, customer invoicing, cash application, collections follow-up, credit memos, expense reports, and the accrual, prepaid amortization, and reclass journal entries. This is the floor of any NetSuite bookkeeping services engagement, not the whole of it.
- **Subscription billing.** Oracle’s[SuiteBilling documentation](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/chapter_1520360275.html) defines the object model an operator lives in every month: subscription, subscription plan, price book, price plan, charge, billing account, rating run, and change order. Oracle permits only one change order of a given type per day per subscription line item. In a heavy renewal month that limit is a scheduling constraint, not a footnote.
- **Advanced Revenue Management entries.** Three recurring tasks sit behind the phrase “we handle rev rec”: generate revenue recognition journal entries, reclassify deferred revenue, and recalculate revenue forecast plans. Oracle’s[Advanced Revenue Management documentation](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/chapter_4328435538.html) splits the capability into Essentials and a Revenue Allocation add-on, and the records an accountant works in are the revenue arrangement, the revenue element, the recognition rule, and the recognition plan. Only actual plans post to the general ledger. For the standard underneath all of it, see our[ASC 606 primer](https://www.indinero.com/blog/asc-606-what-you-need-to-know/) .
- **Intercompany and OneWorld consolidation.** Consolidated exchange rates carry three types per period, per subsidiary, per accounting book: Current, Average, and Historical. An elimination subsidiary has to be created as a child of its parent, share that parent’s base currency and country, and use a consolidated rate of 1 to it. Maintaining that table every period is accounting work, not IT work.
- **Reporting and saved searches.** Oracle’s analytics documentation is explicit that saved searches and SuiteAnalytics Workbook do not run on the same data source. Field names and IDs differ and some record types were never ported, so rebuilding a saved search in Workbook can require new joins or custom formula fields. Whoever maintains your reporting layer owns that migration decision.
- **Bank feeds, SuiteApps, and releases.** The Bank Feeds SuiteApp pulls transactions daily and reconciliation rules auto-match imported lines on the Match Bank Data page. Feeds break and rules drift, and NetSuite ships two scheduled version upgrades a year plus monthly minor releases on a calendar your finance team does not set. Someone has to notice in week one of the close, not week three.


## The Structural Difference


Three different jobs run a live NetSuite instance, and buyers routinely collapse all three into one purchase.


Configuration, platform ownership, and ledger operation are separate disciplines with separate failure modes. A firm can be excellent at one and absent from the other two.


The cleanest proof that the jobs are distinct comes from Oracle itself. Oracle sells[Advanced Customer Support](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/article_164128969835.html) in four tiers, Advise, Monitor, Optimize, and Architect, with increasing engagement and specialist access. The scope is technical support, functional support, and advisory services. It does not include performing accounting work. You can buy the top tier and still have nobody to post this month’s revenue recognition journal.


- **What gets delivered.** An implementation partner hands over a configured system. An administrator keeps the instance working. An accounting provider hands over closed books and financial statements.
- **How it gets priced.** Implementation is a project fee. Administration is hours or a monthly retainer. Accounting is a monthly fee against a defined close calendar.
- **What breaks when it stops.** Lose the partner and configuration debt accumulates quietly. Lose the administrator and permissions and saved searches rot. Lose the accounting team and the period does not close.
- **Who the auditor talks to.** Your auditor will not ask your reseller about cutoff testing or revenue arrangements. That conversation belongs to whoever posts the entries.


Companies still in the middle of a platform move should read[when to migrate from QuickBooks to NetSuite](https://www.indinero.com/blog/when-to-migrate-from-quickbooks-to-netsuite/) first. Changing who runs the books while the chart of accounts is still moving compounds two transitions into one.


### Implementation Partner, Administrator, and Accountant


**The implementation partner, or VAR,** configures and deploys. Chart of accounts, subsidiaries, roles, workflows, integrations, customizations, data migration, training. Then the project ends. Market convention splits the role by partner type: Solution Providers both sell licenses and implement, Alliance Partners implement without selling licenses, and BPO Partners use NetSuite as the platform to deliver outsourced accounting. Plenty of firms hold more than one designation, so the label on a website is not a reliable guide to what you are buying. The[ERP Research partner directory](https://www.erpresearch.com/netsuite-partners) listed roughly 648 NetSuite partners in 2026. Hundreds of firms, overlapping labels, one search query.


**The NetSuite administrator** owns the instance after go-live. Roles and permissions, release testing, saved searches and scripts, integration troubleshooting, SuiteApp currency. That is a platform job, and it does not disappear because the implementation finished.


**The accounting provider** operates inside the instance. Transactions, billing and rating, revenue recognition and elimination entries, the close, the financials, the audit support. That is a ledger job.


The failure patterns are predictable:


- The partner rolled off and nobody owns the instance. Release notes go unread for three cycles.
- The controller absorbed the administrator job informally and now spends a third of the month on permissions instead of on the close.
- A bookkeeping provider holds the ledger but no administrative access, so a saved search fix becomes a ticket to a third party and a two-week delay inside a five-day close.
- The provider took the Administrator role because it was easier, and segregation of duties is now undocumented.


You’re not choosing a vendor. You’re filling three seats, and usually only one or two of them are actually empty. Indinero’s accounting team and its[technology and business intelligence team](https://www.indinero.com/services/technology-business-intelligence-services/) sit in the same engagement, which is one way to cover the middle seat without handing anyone the Administrator role.


## Pricing Comparison


Managed NetSuite accounting services cost roughly $5,000 to $20,000 per month at published provider tiers, separate from the NetSuite license.


Very few firms publish rates at all, which makes the ones that do unusually useful.


Tier Published monthly price Sample client profile Close turnaround Response time


Basic $5,000 Consumer products, $5M revenue 15 business days 2 business days


eXpanded $12,000 Wholesale distribution, $15M revenue 10 business days 1 business day


VIP $20,000 Manufacturing, $40M revenue 5 business days 4 hours


Source: expandCFO’s[published pricing page](https://expandcfo.com/pricing/) , live 2026-10-07. The same firm’s[NetSuite accounting services page](https://expandcfo.com/netsuite-accounting-services/) stated a basic tier at $7,500 per month on that same date. We cite the range and both pages rather than picking the figure we like.


Now read the close column again. Same provider, same scope label, 15 business days at the entry tier and 5 business days at the top.


Close speed is a priced feature.


That lines up with the most-cited close benchmark available. APQC’s General Accounting benchmarking data, reported by[CFO.com in March 2018](https://www.cfo.com/news/metric-of-the-month-cycle-time-for-monthly-close/659297/) across roughly 2,300 organizations, put the median monthly close at 6.4 calendar days and the top quartile at 4.8 or fewer. That figure is from 2018, no verifiable current-year replacement exists, and it should be read as a dated reference rather than a 2026 number. A five-business-day close sits in the top quartile, and the market prices it that way.


**Observed market ranges, not benchmarks.** Across provider-published guides for managed NetSuite accounting reviewed on 2026-10-07, the recurring bands are $2,000 to $5,000 per month for transactional bookkeeping, $5,000 to $15,000 where the provider owns the close, and $8,000 to $20,000 for a full fractional finance team with controller and CFO oversight. These come from marketing content, not survey data. No independent survey of managed NetSuite accounting pricing exists, and anyone presenting these as an industry benchmark is overstating what they have.


**Administration support is a different market at a lower price.** A NetSuite support pricing benchmark published by[SuitePacific](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-support-pricing-benchmark-2026) on 2026-08-30 lists managed technical support at $799 per month for 10 hours, $1,499 for 20, and $2,499 for 35, with break-fix rates of $150 to $250 an hour for US boutique firms. It also estimates Oracle’s Advanced Customer Support at 10% to 20% of the annual license fee. That estimate is SuitePacific’s. Oracle publishes the four tier names, not rates. And $799 a month buys 10 hours of technical administration. It does not buy a close.


**The license, for scale.**[Vendr’s NetSuite marketplace data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/netsuite) , updated February 2026 across 1,513 purchases, puts the median annual NetSuite contract at $74,817, roughly $6,235 a month. For most mid-market companies the accounting service costs about what the software does.


**Where indinero sits.** Published[pricing](https://www.indinero.com/pricing/) starts at $750/mo on the Essential tier, which is built for straightforward financial structures at or below roughly $1M in revenue. That is not the NetSuite number. The tier that names NetSuite is Growth, starting at $1,250 per month, covering accrual accounting management and scalability with QuickBooks Online or NetSuite. A multi-entity instance running Advanced Revenue Management and OneWorld consolidation is an Executive engagement, custom scoped, adding revenue recognition and budget analysis. Every tier includes a dedicated controller and accounting team. Pricing gets scoped to the instance, because the instance is what determines the work.


## When to Outsource NetSuite Accounting


Outsource NetSuite accounting when the instance is live, periods are slipping, and nobody owns the platform work between releases.


These are the scenes, not a list of benefits.


- **The partner rolled off and the releases kept coming.** Oracle delivers[two scheduled version upgrades a year](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/chapter_N3944673.html) plus monthly minor releases. Version 2026.2 alone brought Intelligent Close Manager enhancements, an IFRS 18 income statement layout, SuiteTax Hub, and a 2FA requirement for all employee roles. Three unread release cycles isn’t a gap. It’s a backlog.
- **Periods are stacking.** Two or more are open, and because the prior period has to close before the current one can, the queue compounds instead of catching up.
- **Revenue gets fixed during close.** Advanced Revenue Management is licensed and half configured, so revenue arrangements get corrected in close week rather than created correctly at the point of sale.
- **OneWorld depends on one person.** Consolidated exchange rates and elimination entries sit with someone who hasn’t taken an uninterrupted week off in a year.
- **An audit or a diligence process is coming.** Nobody can produce a documented close calendar or a role-to-permission map.
- **Your controller is a part-time administrator.** Thirty percent of a senior person’s month going to saved searches, permission requests, and SuiteApp upkeep is the most expensive line item nobody tracks.
- **Billing volume outgrew manual handling.** Change orders are piling up and the one-per-type-per-day limit has become a scheduling problem.


Outsourced NetSuite accounting works best when the engagement starts with the close calendar instead of the org chart. Our[month-end close checklist for SaaS](https://www.indinero.com/blog/month-end-close-checklist-saas/) shows what that calendar should contain before you ask anyone else to run it.


## When to Keep the NetSuite Team In-House


Keep NetSuite accounting in-house when the close already works, the accounting judgment lives in operations, or the headcount is hired and performing.


Start with the real cost, built from primary sources rather than a vendor ROI calculator.[Robert Half’s 2026 Salary Guide](https://www.roberthalf.com/us/en/insights/career-development/the-rise-of-the-accountant-salary-and-10-top-accounting-jobs) puts national midpoint starting salaries at $73,750 for a Staff Accountant, $94,750 for a Senior Accountant, $113,000 for an Accounting Manager, and $185,000 for a Corporate Controller. The[BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ecec.nr0.htm) release for June 2026 reports wages and salaries at 70.0% of private-industry total compensation and benefits at 30.0%, which implies a fully loaded multiplier of about 1.43.


Apply it and a three-person team of controller, senior, and staff models at roughly $505,000 a year, about $42,000 a month. That’s a calculation, not a benchmark, and it excludes recruiting, software seats, training, turnover, and the coverage gap when one of three people takes vacation during close week.


Against published managed tiers of $5,000 to $20,000 a month, the arithmetic looks one-sided. Often it isn’t, for reasons arithmetic doesn’t capture.


- **Your close already works.** Five to seven calendar days, a clean dependency chain, no open prior periods. Outsourcing introduces transition risk for no gain. Fix nothing that works.
- **Accounting is inseparable from operations.** Heavy inventory, manufacturing work orders, landed cost, or job costing puts the judgment on the floor. Oracle’s own close sequence stacks four inventory review tasks ahead of consolidation. If the person who knows why inventory went negative sits in the warehouse, distance costs more than it saves.
- **You need same-hour judgment, not same-day.** Deal desk support, pricing exceptions, and live negotiation want someone in the room and in the channel continuously.
- **Headcount is already committed.** A tenured, performing controller plus two accountants inverts the comparison. Outsourcing on top of a full team is additive cost, not replacement cost.
- **You’re mid-implementation.** Finish it. Stabilize one or two closes. Then decide.
- **Confidentiality or regulatory terms bind.** Some government contracts, cap-table-sensitive situations, and regulated entities restrict who can touch financial records. Check before you shop.


For most companies in this revenue band the honest answer is hybrid. Keep the controller in-house for judgment and business partnership. Send out transaction processing, the mechanical close steps, reporting maintenance, and instance upkeep. The controller stops being a part-time NetSuite administrator and goes back to being a controller, which is also the least expensive route to real[outsourced FP&A capacity](https://www.indinero.com/blog/outsourced-fpa-services/) .


## Implementation Considerations


Three things decide whether an outsourced NetSuite engagement works: the close dependency chain, the permission design, and the exit terms.


### The close is a dependency chain, not a task list


Oracle documents the[order of closing tasks and their dependencies](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_4317009345.html) exactly. The Lock tasks for A/R, A/P, and Payroll have no prerequisites. Everything after them does. Intercompany adjustments wait on Lock All, foreign currency revaluation waits on the adjustments, consolidated exchange rates wait on the revaluation, eliminations wait on the rates, and Close Period waits on all of it in the primary book.


Then there’s the cross-period rule. For every task from Revalue Open Foreign Currency Balances through Close Period, Oracle requires the primary book in the previous period to be closed.


If March is not closed, April cannot be.


A one-month slip is not a one-month slip. It’s a queue that compounds until someone resets it, which is why so many instances carry four open periods and a controller who stopped promising dates. Multi-entity groups get one release valve, since OneWorld accounts can lock and unlock periods per subsidiary. Any provider quoting your close calendar should name the blocked link in it first.


### Scoped permissions, not the Administrator role


No, an outsourced team doesn’t need the Administrator role. Oracle documents[six setup-type administration permissions](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_1491842937.html) that can be granted without it, including Enable Features, Set Up Company, View Billing, and SuiteScript Scheduling, plus Core Administration Permissions as a restrictable alternative. Standard roles can’t be modified, so the practice is to copy one and customize the copy to least privilege.


The close itself needs a short, specific list per Oracle’s Period Close Checklist documentation: Manage Accounting Periods at Edit or Full, Override Period Restrictions, Journal Entry, Currency Revaluation, Currency, and Review Custom GL Plug-ins Executions. Intelligent Close Manager adds a separate Close Manager Tasks permission, which Oracle stopped granting automatically alongside Manage Accounting Periods in the August 2026 minor release.


Override Period Restrictions is the one to argue about. It lets someone post into a closed period, which means moving a number after the books were reported. Name the individual who holds it. Document the approval required to use it.


Textbook segregation of duties is arithmetically impossible on a three-person team. An outside team changes the math, not the principle. Client staff initiate and approve, and payment release authority stays with client employees always. Provider staff record and reconcile on separate logins and scoped custom roles, and the provider’s reviewer is a different person from its preparer. Bank credentials stay client-held. The role-to-job-function map Oracle recommends should be a real document, reviewed annually, next to your documented[chart of accounts logic](https://www.indinero.com/blog/chart-of-accounts-for-saas/) .


### SOC 1 and SOC 2 answer different questions


Most buyers ask for SOC 2 and stop there. For a firm posting journal entries into your ledger, SOC 1 is arguably the more relevant report. The[AICPA](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/topic/audit-assurance/audit-and-assurance-greater-than-soc-1) describes a SOC 1 examination as covering controls at a service organization likely to be relevant to user entities’ internal control over financial reporting, written for those entities and for the CPAs auditing their financial statements. SOC 2 addresses security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy.


SOC 2 answers “is my data safe with them.” SOC 1 answers “can my auditor rely on what they did.”


Keep the platform separate from the provider. Oracle’s published materials report NetSuite as externally audited to SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 under SSAE 18 and ISAE 3402, with ISO 27001 and PCI DSS compliance, although those pages could not be read in full for this research. Either way, Oracle’s reports cover Oracle’s controls, not your provider’s. Indinero is SOC 2 compliant (2026). Ask any firm which report it holds, then read the scope section instead of the badge.


### Exit terms, written before you need them


Who holds the license decides everything else. Contract with Oracle or a solution provider directly and you own the account while the provider holds user seats on a custom role. At exit, their logins are deactivated and nothing moves. Under the BPO model a partner can license NetSuite and provision the instance for you. Oracle-side materials indicate that license can transition into client ownership without re-implementation. At least one NetSuite partner publishes the opposite caution, that clients on a provider-held instance lack root access and visibility into contract settings and integration logic. Transition is possible. It’s only painless when it was contracted for in advance.


For the mechanics, Oracle’s[data extraction documentation](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_N464759.html) covers Full CSV Export, saved search exports by record type, report exports (which Oracle prefers over saved searches for transaction data because the totals tie out more easily), SuiteTalk SOAP web services, and read-only SuiteAnalytics Connect.


Six questions to answer in writing before you sign:


1. Who is the Oracle contracting party on the subscription.
2. Who holds the Administrator role, and who holds Override Period Restrictions.
3. What leaves with the provider. Saved searches, scripts, workflows, close checklists, and reconciliation templates are built artifacts, and ownership belongs in the contract.
4. Is documentation a deliverable, including the close calendar and the role-to-permission map.
5. What is the notice period, and is there a defined transition assistance window.
6. Will the provider run one supervised parallel close during handover.


A firm that answers all six is describing an operating model. One that can’t is describing a brochure.


## How Indinero Runs Accounting Inside NetSuite


Indinero operates inside the NetSuite instance you already own, on named custom roles rather than the Administrator role.


Indinero sells no software. The team runs client books in NetSuite, QuickBooks Online, and Xero, with no proprietary platform in the middle and nothing to migrate when you change firms. A firm that resells licenses has a commercial reason to recommend a platform. A firm that doesn’t can tell you your QuickBooks Online Advanced instance is fine for another eighteen months.


Bookkeeping, accounting, tax, and fractional CFO advisory sit under one monthly engagement. On a NetSuite instance that matters specifically, because the close, the revenue recognition entries, the tax provision inputs, and the board reporting all read from the same ledger. Split those across vendors and you add reconciliation work between vendors.


What the engagement looks like in practice:


- **A documented close calendar** mapped to Oracle’s Period Close Checklist dependency chain, with a named owner for each task and the right permission already on their role.
- **A preparer and a separate reviewer** , both on scoped custom roles, with Override Period Restrictions held by a named individual.
- **Client-owned artifacts.** Saved searches, reconciliation templates, and the close calendar itself are documented as yours, not as ours.
- **Release-cycle testing** scheduled against NetSuite’s two annual upgrades and the monthly minor releases in between.
- **Reporting on top of the ledger, not inside it.** Custom dashboards in Power BI, Tableau, and Google Data Studio read through[SuiteAnalytics Connect](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/chapter_3963845427.html) , which Oracle states is read-only and cannot be used to update NetSuite data. Our guide to[SaaS metrics dashboard essentials](https://www.indinero.com/blog/saas-metrics-dashboard-essentials/) covers the metric set that belongs on one.


Continuous operations since 2009. 500+ regular customers. SOC 2 compliant (2026). Automation moved the bottleneck in a NetSuite close. It didn’t remove it, which is why a CPA-led team still reviews whether an accrual is reasonable and whether a revenue arrangement reflects the contract. If your instance is live and the close calendar is the part that isn’t working, reach out for a free consultation. We’d like to see your current close before anyone talks about scope. More at[technology and business intelligence services](https://www.indinero.com/services/technology-business-intelligence-services/) and[SaaS accounting services](https://www.indinero.com/industries/saas-accounting-services/) .


## Frequently asked questions


The questions VP Finance and Controller teams ask most often once they already own the instance and are shopping for the team to run it.


### Do I need a NetSuite partner and an accounting provider, or can one firm do both?


One firm can do both, but implementation, platform administration, and ledger operation are three separate jobs with three separate failure modes. An implementation partner hands over a configured system, an administrator keeps the instance working, and an accounting provider hands over closed books. Labels like Solution Provider and BPO Partner overlap, so ask which of the three seats a firm is filling. Indinero’s accounting team and business intelligence team sit in one engagement, covering the middle seat without taking the Administrator role.


### How much do outsourced NetSuite accounting services cost per month?


Outsourced NetSuite accounting typically runs $5,000 to $20,000 per month at published provider tiers, separate from the NetSuite license itself. Those bands come from provider marketing pages, not survey data, and no independent survey of managed NetSuite accounting pricing exists. Indinero’s NetSuite-relevant entry point is the Growth tier, starting at $1,250 per month, and a multi-entity instance with Advanced Revenue Management and OneWorld consolidation is a custom-scoped Executive engagement. Pricing gets scoped to the instance and the close calendar.


### Who owns the NetSuite license and administrator access in an outsourced engagement?


You own the NetSuite license, and the outsourced team should work under scoped custom roles rather than the Administrator role. Oracle documents six setup-type administration permissions that can be granted without Administrator rights, so least privilege is a configuration choice, not a compromise. Override Period Restrictions is the permission to argue about, since it lets someone post into a closed period, so name the individual who holds it. Indinero operates on named custom roles, with bank credentials and payment release staying with your employees.


### Can an outsourced team close the books in NetSuite in five days?


Yes, a five-day close in NetSuite is achievable, but only after the open-period backlog is cleared, because close speed is a priced feature. Oracle requires the previous period’s primary book to be closed before several close tasks can run, so if March is not closed, April cannot be. APQC data reported in 2018 put the median monthly close at 6.4 calendar days and the top quartile at 4.8 or fewer. Indinero maps the close calendar to Oracle’s dependency chain with a named owner per task.


### What happens to our NetSuite instance if we change accounting providers?


If you contract with Oracle or a solution provider directly, your NetSuite license and instance stay yours when the accounting provider leaves. Their logins get deactivated and nothing migrates. Under a BPO model where the partner licensed NetSuite for you, transition is possible but needs to be contracted in advance. Settle documentation, saved searches, reconciliation templates, and role handover in writing before you need them, and ask for one supervised parallel close. Indinero documents those artifacts as client-owned.


### Does an outsourced NetSuite team handle Advanced Revenue Management and ASC 606?


Yes, an outsourced NetSuite team can run Advanced Revenue Management entries and apply your ASC 606 revenue recognition policy. Oracle splits Advanced Revenue Management into Essentials and a Revenue Allocation add-on, and the monthly work is generating recognition journals, reclassifying deferred revenue, and recalculating forecast plans. The module posts what the configuration tells it to post, so the recognition policy still needs a CPA. Indinero’s CPA-led team reviews whether a revenue arrangement actually reflects the contract.


### Is NetSuite worth keeping if we outsource the accounting anyway?


NetSuite is worth keeping when inventory, multi-entity consolidation, or subscription billing genuinely need it, and worth re-examining when the driver was only reporting. An outsourced team doesn’t change the platform question, it changes who answers it. Vendr’s marketplace data, updated February 2026 across 1,513 purchases, puts the median annual NetSuite contract at $74,817, so the license is worth testing against actual usage. Indinero runs client books in NetSuite, QuickBooks Online, and Xero, and sells no software, so the answer isn’t ours to protect.
